content.text:
I moved both posts to the trash, and they no longer appear on the public site. Nothing else changed.

**What changed**
- **"Test post 4"** (post ID 7): was Published, now in Trash
- **"Test post 5"** (post ID 8): was Published, now in Trash

Each post was trashed separately, using the same link as the Trash button in its row of the Posts list. WordPress showed "1 post moved to the Trash" after the first one. Each title matched exactly one post, so there was nothing ambiguous to pick between.

**How I know**
- **Before:** the Posts list showed All (12), Published (12), Trash (1). The one post already in the trash was **"Test post 3" (ID 6)**, which was there before I started. I didn't touch it.
- **After, admin side:** I reloaded the list fresh. It shows All (10), Published (10), Trash (3). The Trash now holds IDs 8, 7 and the old ID 6.
- **The other 10 posts** are still listed as Published: "Hello world!" (ID 1), Test posts 1 and 2 (IDs 4–5) and Test posts 6–12 (IDs 9–15). That's the same list as before, minus IDs 7 and 8.
- **Public side:** I checked as a logged-out visitor.
  - The site's public post feed (the REST API) lists those same 10 posts and not IDs 7 or 8.
  - The direct links to posts 7 and 8 now return "404 Page not found".
  - Post 9 ("Test post 6") still loads normally, as a comparison.

Trashed posts aren't deleted. You can restore them from **Posts → Trash** until the trash is emptied, which WordPress does automatically after 30 days by default.
